rest.label: rest, with as little effort as possible

hands-on.label: actually cooking something, with your hands busy

sweet.label: a little sweetness, an evening kind of comfort

pantry.label: making do with what's already in the cupboard

window.label: The rain
window.moment: It's properly coming down. The glass is all streaks.

armchair.label: The armchair
armchair.moment: Sagging in exactly the right places. The blanket's still warm.

plant.label: The plant
plant.moment: Somebody's been talking to it. It's doing well.

oil-lamp.label: The lamp
oil-lamp.moment: A small, steady light. The kind you read by.

cutting-board.label: Chopping board
cutting-board.moment: Knife marks from a thousand onions.

bowl.label: The bowl
bowl.moment: A wide, heavy bowl. Holds warmth well.

basket.label: The basket
basket.moment: Half a loaf, wrapped in a tea towel.

atoms.title: Honey, ginger and lemon in a mug
atoms.body: A few slices of ginger, a squeeze of lemon, a spoon of honey, hot (not boiling) water. Wrap both hands round it. That's the whole recipe.

atoms.title: Five-minute miso broth
atoms.body: Stir a spoon of miso into a mug of hot water off the boil. Add whatever's soft and easy: tofu cubes, a handful of spinach, leftover rice. Sip it slowly.

atoms.title: Buttered toast, cut into soldiers
atoms.body: Toast counts. You're eating, and that's the win. Cutting it into strips somehow makes it feel like someone's looking after you.

atoms.title: Overnight oats for tomorrow-you
atoms.body: Half a cup of oats, the same of milk, a spoon of honey, into a jar and into the fridge. Future-you wakes up to breakfast already made.

atoms.title: Slow rice congee
atoms.body: A little rice, a lot of stock, a low heat and an hour of the house smelling wonderful. Ginger and spring onion on top. Perfect for a rainy afternoon when you can potter.

atoms.title: Why ginger feels warming
atoms.body: That gentle heat comes from compounds like gingerol, the same family of molecules behind chilli's kick, just softer. It's why a ginger tea feels like it warms you from the middle out.

atoms.title: Why warm food feels like comfort
atoms.body: Warm, soft, salty food is easy to eat when your appetite is low, and the steam and smell do half the work before you've taken a spoonful. Comfort is a real thing, not a weakness.

atoms.title: The rainy-day soup pot
atoms.body: Onion, carrot and celery, slowly softened in butter, then whatever vegetables need using and enough stock to cover. Let it tick over while the rain does its thing.

atoms.title: What "spoons" means
atoms.body: Spoon theory: on some days you only have a few units of energy to spend. Knowing your count is how you choose a meal that doesn't cost more than you've got.

atoms.title: No-chop pantry pasta
atoms.body: Pasta, a tin of tomatoes, a glug of oil, salt, and a pinch of dried herbs. Nothing to chop, one pot, fifteen minutes.

atoms.title: Green herb salt
atoms.body: Chop a big handful of soft herbs with flaky salt until it's bright green and damp. A pinch of it wakes up eggs, rice, anything plain.

atoms.title: Cucumber and mint water
atoms.body: A jug of cold water, a few cucumber ribbons, a sprig of mint, a slice of lemon. It feels like more effort than it is.

atoms.title: Gentle knife skills: the claw
atoms.body: Curl your fingertips under, knuckles forward, so the blade rides against your knuckles. Slow is fine. Chopping can be oddly calming once it feels safe.

atoms.title: Warm milk with cinnamon
atoms.body: Milk (any kind) warmed in a pan with a pinch of cinnamon and a little honey. Drink it by lamplight. It's not magic, it's a signal to yourself that the day is done.

atoms.title: One baked apple
atoms.body: Core an apple, fill it with oats, butter and honey, and bake until it slumps. The kitchen smells like autumn for an hour.

atoms.title: Good bread, good butter, a little salt
atoms.body: Sometimes the best thing in the basket needs nothing doing to it. Thick slice, real butter, a few flakes of salt.

atoms.title: Stock from scraps
atoms.body: Keep onion ends, carrot peels and herb stalks in a bag in the freezer. When it's full, cover with water and simmer for an hour. Free broth, and nothing wasted.

atoms.title: What a squeeze of lemon does
atoms.body: Acid makes flavours taste brighter and more distinct, which is why a squeeze of lemon can rescue a flat soup. Add it at the end, off the heat.

atoms.title: An armchair plate
atoms.body: Crackers, a bit of cheese, apple slices, a few nuts. Nothing cooked, nothing to wash but one plate, and you can eat it with a blanket over your knees.

atoms.title: A note on honey
atoms.body: Honey's flavour changes with whatever the bees were visiting: clover is mild, mānuka is deep and bitter-edged. One firm rule: never give honey to babies under a year old.
